relevance_reason: Reports DCTN1 missense variants in ALS patients rather than in distal hereditary motor neuronopathy. It gives allelic context for the gene in this entry but does not characterise HMND14 itself.

findings.statement: Münch et al. (2004) screened the DCTN1 and cytoplasmic dynein heavy chain (DNCHC1) genes in 250 patients with ALS and 150 unrelated controls. They found heterozygous missense mutations in DCTN1 in 3 patients: T1249I in 1 apparently sporadic ALS case, M571T in 1 person with familial ALS, and R785W in 2 patients with familial ALS from 1 kindred. The R785W variant was also present in 2 unaffected relatives from that kindred. The authors suggested that DCTN1 allelic variants may be a previously unknown genomic risk factor for ALS.
quotes: The authors report mutation screening of the p150 subunit of dynactin (DCTN1) and the cytoplasmic dynein heavy chain (DNCHC1) genes in 250 patients with ALS and 150 unrelated control subjects.

Heterozygous missense mutations of the DCTN1 gene were detected in one apparently sporadic case of ALS (T1249I), one individual with familial ALS (M571T), two patients with familial ALS, and two unaffected relatives in the same kindred (R785W).
The allelic variants of the DCTN1 gene may represent a previously unknown genomic risk factor for ALS.

relevance_reason: This is the original report that linked a lower motor neuron disease to 2p13 and found a dynactin (DCTN1) missense mutation that reduces microtubule binding.

findings.statement: Puls et al. (2003) showed linkage of a lower motor neuron disease to a 4-Mb region on chromosome 2p13.
quotes: Here we show linkage of a lower motor neuron disease to a region of 4 Mb at chromosome 2p13.

findings.statement: In a lower motor neuron disease linked to 2p13, Puls et al. (2003) analyzed the gene encoding the largest subunit of the axonal transport protein dynactin. They found a single base-pair change that causes an amino acid substitution, which is predicted to distort the folding of dynactin's microtubule-binding domain.
quotes: Mutation analysis of a gene in this interval that encodes the largest subunit of the axonal transport protein dynactin showed a single base-pair change resulting in an amino-acid substitution that is predicted to distort the folding of dynactin's microtubule-binding domain.

variants.as_reported: single base-pair change resulting in an amino-acid substitution

findings.statement: In binding assays by Puls et al. (2003), the mutant dynactin protein bound less to microtubules. The authors concluded that dysfunction of dynactin-mediated transport can lead to human motor neuron disease.
quotes: Binding assays show decreased binding of the mutant protein to microtubules.
Our results show that dysfunction of dynactin-mediated transport can lead to human motor neuron disease.
